fields.reasoning: Intent: the evidence is a Nebari plan run (01M6VY5APJP9, PR #78) blocked by a Rails flake, and the closest precedent, the ci-triage RSpec fix (01M6TB6N, decision-ci-triage-runners), served m27-nebari-on-rhiza ('Nebari's daemon builds and ships a Nebari change set on its own with Rhiza's workflows'); a plan run that dies on an unrelated flake is the same blocker. Rerun: internal/api/ship.go shipRerunFailed stops after one rerun per head (st.RerunHead == resp.Commit && len(st.Reruns) > 0), and plan.toml's pr-green and rebased-green just run 'rhiza ship check', so the run fails on the second red; the question notes the first rerun already fired and failed and a third attempt passed, so the plan needs a second rerun per head, not the first. A budgeted flag on ship check keeps it deterministic, bounded and visible in the workflow file, leaves ship-change and ci-rerun-once-per-head unchanged by default, and avoids an agent step for a plan whose diff is only .rhiza/. Naming: ship check already parses failing tests from --log-failed (parseFailedTests, shipReadFailures), so reusing it names the test; the 'unrelated' claim is made only when the diff really is .rhiza-only, so it is true whichever workflow calls it. Failing: the change set's intent says 'rerun the failed jobs once (budgeted) and only then fail', and merging on red would bypass the repo's required checks and could hide a real break on main; the reruns absorb ordinary flakes and a persistent red is worth the owner's eye, now with a message that says it is not the plan's fault.
fields.statement: Change set 01M6WHT serves intent m27-nebari-on-rhiza (01M6J303FW4PYT5E5CE39QNHJ8). (1) Rerun budget: rhiza ship check takes a --reruns <n> flag (default 1, today's ci-rerun-once-per-head behaviour; n >= 1) that reruns a head's failed Actions jobs up to n times per head, each rerun recorded in the ship record (a per-head count beside RerunHead/Reruns) before gh run rerun --failed is called, so a crash costs a missed rerun, never an extra one; plan.toml passes --reruns 2 to every ship check in wait-pr, pr-green, wait-rebased and rebased-green, giving a plan PR three CI attempts per head; ship-change keeps the default, since its red CI goes to ci-triage and ci-fix. No agent step and no change to max_visits. (2) Naming: when a check is still red once the head's reruns are spent, ship check reads the failed runs' logs as it does for ci-triage and its error names each failed check and the failing tests it parsed (or says none could be read); when the PR's diff from its merge base touches only .rhiza/ paths, the error adds that the PR changes only .rhiza/, so the failure is unrelated to the plan (a flaky or broken test on main), for example: 'check test (4/5) failed on 18230d2 after 2 reruns: rspec ./spec/system/garden_location_spec.rb[1:1:11]; the PR changes only .rhiza/, so this failure is unrelated to the plan'. (3) Yes: a .rhiza-only PR whose checks stay red after the reruns still fails the step and ends the run failed; Rhiza never merges past a red check. The run's inbox item carries that message, and the owner resumes with gh run rerun --failed and rhiza run resume --retry as today.
